Automatic annotation of cell types

AnnotateCells.Rd

This function transfers cell type annotations from a reference Seurat dataset to a query Seurat dataset using non-negative least squares ("nnls", default) or Seurat anchor transfer ("Seurat"). For each column specified in reference_groups, a corresponding column of predicted cell type annotations and a <group>_score column of per-cell prediction scores are added to the metadata of the query dataset. In addition, one can optionally summarize these annotations for a specific clustering solution, which adds a <group>_summary column containing the most common annotation per cluster.

Usage

AnnotateCells(
  object,
  reference = reference,
  summarize_by_column = NULL,
  reference_assay = "PNA",
  query_assay = "PNA",
  reference_groups = c("celltype.l1", "celltype.l2"),
  normalization_method = c("CLR", "LogNormalize", "SCT"),
  reduction = "cca",
  method = c("nnls", "Seurat", "nmf"),
  min_prediction_score = 0,
  predict_doublets = FALSE,
  min_doublet_score = 0.4,
  skip_normalization = FALSE,
  verbose = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

Seurat object to which you want to add celltype annotation

reference

Seurat object that contains annotated reference data, see read_pbmc_reference and examples for obtaining a PBMC reference dataset

summarize_by_column

If NULL, return only the cell type annotation per cell. If the name of a column in the object metadata is provided, the annotations will be summarized to the factors of this column, i.e. the most common annotation per factor level will be retained. Useful for annotating the output of the Seurat clustering, for example, Default: NULL

reference_assay

Assay in the reference dataset used for annotation, Default: 'PNA'

query_assay

Assay in the query dataset used for annotation, Default: 'PNA'

reference_groups

A character vector of reference metadata columns to use for annotation, Default: c("celltype.l1", "celltype.l2")

normalization_method

Normalization method used prior to annotation (with margin = 2), either "CLR", "LogNormalize", or "SCT", Default: 'CLR'

reduction

Reduction method used during FindTransferAnchors when method = "Seurat", Default: 'cca'

method

Method to use for annotation, either "nnls", "Seurat", or "nmf" (alias for "nnls"), Default: 'nnls'

min_prediction_score

Minimum prediction score for the annotation to be considered valid. Labels with a prediction score below this value will be labelled as "Unknown", Default: 0, meaning that no threshold is used.

predict_doublets

If TRUE, compute a heterotypic doublet score and candidate cell type pair using the first group in reference_groups when method = "nnls", adding doublet_score and doublet_pair columns to the object metadata, Default: FALSE

min_doublet_score

Minimum doublet score required to report a candidate cell type pair in doublet_pair when predict_doublets = TRUE. Cells with a doublet score below this threshold will have doublet_pair set to NA, Default: 0.4

skip_normalization

If TRUE, the datasets will not be normalized prior to annotation. The default layer will be used, so use this setting at your own risk, Default: FALSE

verbose

If TRUE, print messages about the progress of the annotation, Default: TRUE

...

Additional parameters passed to FindTransferAnchors when method = "Seurat"

Value

The initial Seurat object with additional annotation columns added to its metadata.

Details

The "nnls" (or "nmf") method projects query cells onto feature-weighted reference cell type profiles using non-negative least squares (RcppML::project), followed by local fine-tuning across the top candidate cell types. The "Seurat" method is a wrapper for the FindTransferAnchors and TransferData functions from Seurat. Both methods support an optional summary per cluster.

Merged SeuratObject v5 assays (Assay5, including PNAAssay5) must not retain split merge layers (counts.1, data.1, etc.). Run JoinLayers() on the Seurat object (or on the assay) after merge() before calling AnnotateCells().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
reference <- read_pbmc_reference()

seur <- ReadPNA_Seurat(minimal_pna_pxl_file())

seur <- AnnotateCells(
  seur,
  reference = reference
)
} # }
